tabelline on the Nim forum

The post that announces tabelline 0.1 on the Nim forum: first as it will look, then the text to paste. Comment on it with ✎ Review.

Version 5 · updated 10 November 2026, with your edits

Title: tabelline: beautiful display tables for Nim · Category: Project Showcase. The three images are in this page's branch, linked by commit, so their addresses keep working after the merge.

The post

Hi, I just released tabelline 0.1, beautiful display tables for Nim:

https://pietroppeter.github.io/tabelline/

Display tables are tables designed for human consumption (on a website, in a report, on a newspaper...) and are an output of a data process and they are not intended for further consumption.

Tabelline follows R's gt and Python's Great Tables: the same parts of a table and the same verbs in camelCase, written in plain Nim. Tables render to HTML, text and Markdown, and go straight into a nimib page. Further releases are planned to cover more or less the complete feature set and possibly also extend it (styling with a page theme is already something not in the originals, a clean Munari/Japan colors style and a playful Quaderno style are present). The name comes from le tabelline, the times tables of Italian primary school (it also means, small tables).

On the site you find a Guide, a Book that ports the gt and Great Tables guides, stories told with tables (Milano Cortina 2026 and FOSDEM), the roadmap, a devlog and a design guide.

As a small celebration I put every NimConf schedule, 2020 to 2026, in tabelline tables:

https://pietroppeter.github.io/claude-artifacts/nimconf-schedules/

That page also has a review mode for nimib pages: press ✎ Review, select some text, comment, and export all the comments to paste to a coding agent. It will move to nimib, so every nimib notebook can have it.

Made with Claude, mostly from my phone.

I really enjoyed working on this: the reference API is beautiful and I think every language deserves a port of it! The moment I had the idea of the review mode (yesterday morning) it was pretty clear, and it was so much fun iterating on it while using it (see the devlog post: https://pietroppeter.github.io/tabelline/devlog/review-mode/).

To check before posting

  • Images: the forum takes .. image:: url (reStructuredText). If it shows the line instead of the image, use a plain link.
  • FOSDEM: its story is merged but not on the site yet (stories/ lists only Milano Cortina for now): check before posting.
  • Links: gt and Great Tables are Markdown links. If the forum shows the brackets, use bare URLs.
